name: Nouvelle Droite
summary: The Nouvelle Droite is a school of thought, born around the GRECE think-tank in 1968, that treats liberalism as the main enemy and defends rooted communities, cultural difference and a federal, multipolar order. It rejects racial hierarchy, favours restricting immigration while recognising settled communities, and asks for participatory democracy, subsidiarity, ecological limits and a third economic sector.
scope: The mature GRECE synthesis in the 1999 Manifesto for a European Renaissance by Alain de Benoist and Charles Champetier, read with scholarship on the movement. It excludes earlier racialist phases, Faye's later archeofuturism, Dugin and the Alt-Right.

sources.title: Hegemonia cultural y estrategia metapolitica en la derecha radical: la Nueva Derecha Europea y la Alt-Right
sources.author: Ismael Seijo Boado and Lorien Gomez Solano
sources.usedFor: Scholarly account of the movement's worldview, federal Europe, right to difference and paganism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Endorses a central bank, placed under European political authority (III.6).

abortion-legal.rationale: Lists abortion among the specifically feminine rights that differentialist feminism upholds (III.4).

accelerate-technology.rationale: Says innovation is not desirable for its novelty and that technology should follow ethical and political choices under a principle of prudence (II.7).

algorithmic-government.rationale: Says politics is an art of prudence, not something to hand to technology, and attacks the technocratic management of society (II.4, I.3).

alienated-labor.rationale: Describes monetised heteronomous work done from obligation, not vocation, and modernity's generalised alienation (II.3, III.8).

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Rejects the melting pot and strictly assimilationist policy, asking that ethnocultural identity be recognised publicly (III.2, III.3).

basic-income.rationale: Proposes that a minimum income for every citizen from birth to death without return be explored (III.8); a proposal to study, not a firm programme.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Values intermediary bodies and communities between individual and state, though it finds parties discredited (II.3, III.7).

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Grants modern development met basic needs but calls the ideology of progress in crisis and says capitalism trivialised equality (I.2, II.5).

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Says freedom of opinion allows no exceptions and attacks censors of ideas (III.13).

central-bank-independence.rationale: Wants the central bank under the control of European political authority (III.6).

central-planning.rationale: Names ineffective governmental economies one half of an impasse, the other being hyper-competitive markets (III.9).

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: Says traditions are never frozen but constantly renewed (III.10).

character-from-environment.rationale: Holds that individuals carry hereditary predispositions and also a social environment, and rejects stressing either alone (II.1).

civilizational-union.rationale: States that the future belongs to large civilisations organising into autonomous entities and that Europe must federate (III.6, II.8).

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Describes Westernisation of the planet as an imperialist movement imposing a supposedly superior model (II.8).

class-struggle-history.rationale: Says the economy has never been society's infrastructure and that economism is the exception, and gives ideas a fundamental historical role (Introduction, II.5).

clerical-rule.rationale: Holds that politics cannot be reduced to the sacred and that sovereignty rests with the people (II.4, III.7).

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Treats colonialism as part of Western imperialism that erases otherness (II.8).

common-currency.rationale: Says a single currency ought to be managed by a central bank under European political authority (III.6).

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Rejects the hypercompetitive liberal, racist or nationalist view of life as perpetual struggle and the ideology of progress (II.2, I.3).

consent-of-governed.rationale: Holds the people the ultimate holder of sovereignty, rulers subordinate to their will and each level resting on participants' consent (II.4, III.6).

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Argues that the artificial growth of needs ends in an impasse and that being matters more than having (II.5, III.12).

corporate-influence.rationale: Condemns lobbyists upholding private interests over the common good and asks to separate wealth from political power (III.7).

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Attacks the liberal republic of judges and holds the people sovereign, yet protects minorities' freedom of expression (I.3, III.7).

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Treats cultures as different answers to essential questions and the imposition of a supposedly superior model as ethnocentrism, denying any outside yardstick for ranking (II.2, II.8, III.2).

decide-locally.rationale: Subsidiarity is the keystone at every level: communities decide for themselves and higher bodies take only what lower ones cannot manage (II.4, III.5, III.6).

delink-world-market.rationale: Calls for self-sufficiency, an end to the international division of labour and freedom from IMF dictates (III.9).

democracy-becomes-oligarchy.rationale: Treats the democratic crisis as a set of curable aberrations to be met by participation (III.7).

democracy-best.rationale: Calls democracy the only form of government giving citizens a part in public decisions and the one best suited to pluralism (II.4, III.7).

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Says democracy is popular sovereignty and decision for the common good, not the party system or liberal parliamentarism (III.7).

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: Says democracy exists to allow peaceful confrontation of differing worldviews (II.4, III.7).

destroy-worshipped-objects.rationale: Upholds native religions and the sacred's return (III.1, II.9).

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Names communism's regimes the most murderous totalitarian ones and says the Leninist seizure of power now leads nothing (I.2, III.7).

direct-votes.rationale: Says the referendum procedure could also be useful within a participatory democracy (III.7).

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Says social richness grows with diversity of members yet warns of excesses and of immigration's brutal changes to host environments (II.3, III.3).

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Holds the people, not God, the source of power's legitimacy (III.7).

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: Rejects any hierarchy of peoples and any civilisation claiming a redeeming mission (II.8, III.2).

duties-before-rights.rationale: Holds that rights make sense only within a community that attaches duties to them, and that belonging is prior to the individual (II.3, II.6).

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Gives priority to self-sufficiency and internal markets but condemns colonialism and Westernisation as imperialism (III.9, II.8).

elective-rulers.rationale: Locates legitimacy in the people and wants governors and governed as identical as possible (III.7).

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Says equality of all human beings is apolitical and that worth comes from one's own qualities, yet denies any racial hierarchy and affirms equal value of the sexes (III.2, III.4, III.7).

ethnic-nation.rationale: The manifesto proposes a communitarian model for immigrants already settled and rejects both exclusion and assimilation, while the scholarship reads the movement as seeking ethnically homogeneous blocs (III.3; Seijo and Gomez).

evolved-behavioural-sex-differences.rationale: Holds humans bear inherited predispositions and a masculine and feminine nature (II.1, III.4).

exit-over-voice.rationale: Treats participation and voting as the substance of democracy, saying non-voting robs it of meaning (III.7).

experts-over-public.rationale: Attacks the managerial New Class and technocratic rule, insisting politics is an art of prudence and not a science (I.3, II.4, III.5).

femininity-compatible-with-feminism.rationale: Backs a differentialist feminism and criticises admitting women only if they shed femininity (III.4).

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Lists an international tax on all financial transactions among first steps (III.9).

free-trade.rationale: Calls for an end to the international division of labour and priority for internal and regional markets, and rejects a Europe that is only a free-trade market (III.6, III.9).

future-generations.rationale: Sets a principle of responsibility: leave future generations a world no less beautiful, rich or diverse (III.12).

gender-social-construct.rationale: Rejects the universalist-feminist claim that gender is a social construct and holds that a feminine and a masculine nature are evident (III.4).

holocaust-denial.rationale: Lists genocide and mass murder among the results of the twentieth-century ideologies including Nazism (I.2).

human-decline-since-golden-age.rationale: Rejects linear histories with a golden age as starting point, treating past and future as permanent present (II.9).

human-enhancement.rationale: Warns that techno-science manipulating man himself (cloning, artificial procreation) makes him an extension of his tools (II.7).

individual-rights-only.rationale: Says no right exists for isolated individuals and upholds the rights of peoples to their difference (II.6, III.1).

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Calls modernity the emptiest civilisation yet, but concedes development met the basic needs of far more people (I.2, II.5).

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Says Europeans' right to autonomy does not oblige all peoples to guarantee rights alike and rejects exporting one model (II.6, II.8).

keep-public-institutions-small.rationale: Opposes gigantism and wants life at local scale with institutions near the people (III.10).

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Says politics cannot be reduced to the sacred and rejects any absolute eternal law as basis of moral or political choices (II.2, II.4).

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Speaks of the obsolescence of Left and Right and seeks a synthesis borrowing what is valuable from all currents (Introduction).

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: Asks for the widest possible separation between wealth and political power (III.7).

limit-growth.rationale: States that in a finite world there are limits to growth and rejects the ideology of unlimited progress (II.5, III.12).

local-production.rationale: Favours local production and consumption of food and priority for internal and regional markets (III.9, III.12).

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Says economic over-determination is the exception and that ideas play a fundamental role in history (II.5, Introduction).

minority-language-support.rationale: Upholds languages and regional cultures threatened with extinction (III.1).

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Upholds regional cultures and the autonomy of every component of a federal Europe (III.1, III.6).

minority-veto.rationale: Describes majority rule through the vote as the technique for agreement between people and leaders (III.7).

multipolar-world.rationale: Predicts and endorses a multipolar world of civilisations, with power as capacity to resist others (II.8).

nation-first.rationale: Condemns chauvinistic nationalism and a Europe of nations as mere national egos, while favouring cooperation (III.1, III.6).

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Proposes a communitarian model letting immigrants keep the structures of their collective cultural life under common laws (III.3).

national-mission.rationale: Names as the pluriverse's main enemy any civilisation that claims a redeeming universal mission, citing Manifest Destiny (II.8).

natural-rulers.rationale: States that the difference between governors and governed can never be a difference of quality (III.7).

nature-as-capital.rationale: Faults economics for counting only the quantifiable and wants non-quantifiable elements restored (II.5).

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Asks for a move beyond anthropocentrism and describes nature as a partner towards which man has obligations (III.12).

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Says communism betrayed and capitalism trivialised equality and seeks a way out of the double impasse through a third sector (I.2, III.9).

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rejects the neutral liberal state and says public life affirms a vision of the good and an economy embedded in society (I.3, II.4, II.5).

no-central-bank.rationale: Wants a single currency run by a central bank under political authority (III.6).

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Holds that a feminine nature exists though individuals may diverge (III.4).

one-party-rule.rationale: Holds that politics requires a plurality of goals and worldviews and that regimes denying it are unpolitical; democracy is the people's sovereignty (II.4, III.7).

open-borders.rationale: A call for restrictive immigration policy contradicts eventually open borders (III.3).

participatory-democracy.rationale: Demands a true participatory democracy at every level, radically decentralised from the bottom (III.7).

party-controls-media.rationale: Demands total freedom of expression and condemns the thought police of the media (III.13).

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Calls both traditional sexism and the neutralising of sexual difference forms of male domination that excluded or conditionally admitted women (III.4).

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Describes the New Class as inclined to corruption and nepotism and cut off from ordinary citizens, with technocracy and lobbying eroding democracy (III.5, III.7).

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Says politics cannot be reduced to ethics or the sacred and that man is neither good nor bad (II.2, II.4).

pollution-taxes.rationale: States that polluting firms should be taxed in proportion to damage done (III.12).

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Calls for binding international norms and environmental laws besides polluter taxes (III.12, III.9).

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Wants Europe organised as a federation whose summit decides diplomacy, defence, big economic issues and law, with a common currency (III.6).

population-transfer.rationale: Calls mass departure of settled immigrants illusory and refuses both exclusion and assimilation (III.2, III.3).

positive-liberty.rationale: Says modernity's freedom is purely formal and that it proclaims rights without the means to exercise them (I.2).

precautionary-principle.rationale: Says technological development should follow anticipation under the principle of prudence (II.7).

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defends peoples, languages and regional cultures against extinction and wants popular traditions renewed (III.1, III.10), though it speaks of cultures more than of nations.

production-for-use.rationale: Contrasts economics, which serves human needs, with chrematistics aimed at money, and wants the economy back in service of people (III.9).

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: Treats the West's export of political principles and human rights as ethnocentric imperialism (II.8).

promote-ethnic-return-migration.rationale: Calls the departure en masse of resident immigrants illusory and proposes a model for them to stay (III.3).

property-franchise.rationale: Makes democratic equality a political equality of all citizens through membership (III.7).

punish-blasphemy.rationale: States freedom of opinion allows no exceptions and denounces modern Torquemadas (III.13).

race-social-construct.rationale: Says racism is not defeated by negating the concept of races, and that races differ on statistical criteria (III.2).

racial-franchise.rationale: Bases citizenship on belonging and political equality and refuses exclusion (III.2, III.7).

racial-segregation-law.rationale: States the rejection of both exclusion and assimilation: neither apartheid nor the melting pot (III.2).

reason-over-faith.rationale: Rejects instrumental reason as sole guide, calls for the return of the sacred and for reuniting myth and logic (I.1, II.9).

reduce-immigration.rationale: States that the New Right favours policies restrictive of immigration, calling present immigration undeniably negative (III.3).

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: States local economies must be freed from the dictates of the World Bank and IMF (III.9).

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Says each level's role is not derived from approval above but from the consent of its participants (III.6).

reification.rationale: Names the reification of social relations and the fetishism of commodities as products of modern capitalism (II.5, III.5).

religion-from-peoples-character.rationale: Upholds native religions and says cultures answer essential questions differently (III.1, II.2).

religion-illusion.rationale: Calls the sacred an anthropological constant manifest in all religions and expects its return (II.9).

religious-offensive-war.rationale: Cites the Crusades as an example of universalist conversion by force that it condemns (II.8).

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: Upholds peoples, languages and native religions under threat and the right to difference (III.1).

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Refuses both exclusion and assimilation and calls mass departure illusory (III.2, III.3).

restore-past-order.rationale: Says modernity will be overcome not by returning to the past but by pre-modern values in a postmodern setting (I.2).

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Insists on total freedom of expression and rejects productivist growth (III.13, III.8).

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Holds freedom of opinion to allow no exceptions and strongly supports total freedom of expression (III.13).

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Asks to drastically revise the system of economic development and cancel Third World debt (III.9).

return-to-foraging.rationale: Rules out a return to the past as the way beyond modernity (I.2).

return-to-pre-conversion-religion.rationale: Declares sympathy with ancient pagan thought, seeks a return to founding myths and upholds native religions (II.9, III.1; Seijo and Gomez).

sacred-ruler.rationale: Makes the people the ultimate holder of sovereignty, rulers always subordinate to it (II.4).

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Wants popular traditions revived and keeps a long memory of origins (III.10, II.9).

say-in-proportion-to-effect.rationale: Wants local communities to decide what concerns them directly (III.5, III.7).

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Declares sympathy for an ancient pagan worldview and rejects revealed universal truth and the created/uncreated divide (I.1, II.9).

self-interest-moral.rationale: Criticises the liberal individual maximising his own interest and ranks unselfishness over greed among the virtues (I.3, II.6).

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Calls the distinction of the sexes the first and most fundamental natural difference (III.4).

shared-human-nature.rationale: Affirms a human nature all share yet derives rights from social context, not from it (II.2, II.6).

simple-living.rationale: Sets being above having and criticises the artificial multiplication of needs (II.5, III.12).

single-common-good.rationale: Says the goals of social life are always multiple and politics is not a science of reason, though authority aims at a common good (II.4).

single-official-language.rationale: Upholds threatened languages and the right to difference (III.1).

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rejects Bodin's unlimited sovereignty and Leviathan in favour of Althusius's federation of communities (II.4).

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Lists cancelling the debt of Third World countries among the first steps (III.9).

spiritual-nature.rationale: Says man finds meaning by adhering to something greater and expects the sacred's return, while keeping politics distinct (II.9, II.4).

state-harmful.rationale: Treats the state as a federation of communities and names civil peace its first aim (II.4).

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Expects the return of the sacred and treats the religious impulse as an anthropological constant (II.9).

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: States that the public sphere always affirms a vision of the good life and the good precedes the just (II.4).

suppress-opposition.rationale: Defends pluralism, minorities' freedom of expression and total freedom of expression (III.7, III.13).

surveillance-ok.rationale: Links social transparency to totalitarian surveillance and criticises monitored neighbourhoods (II.4, III.11).

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Criticises the belief that more technology will rectify the defects of existing technology and says techno-science has cost life its reason for living (II.7).

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Wants pre-modern values in a postmodern dimension and rejects both technophobia and technophilia (I.2, II.7).

total-state.rationale: Traces absolutism and Jacobinism to totalitarianism and sets against them a federation of autonomous communities (II.4).

traditional-family.rationale: Names the extended family as society's oldest association and wants families to regain their role in education and mutual support (II.3, III.10).

universal-morality.rationale: Holds ethical categories universal but rejects any absolute universal law and Kantian universal morality as a basis for rights (II.2, II.6).

vanguard-party.rationale: Says the Leninist seizure of power leads nowhere in a world of networks (III.7).

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Asks for the widest separation between wealth and political power against money's overwhelming power (III.7).

women-suffrage.rationale: Condemns the exclusion of women from public life and wants them fully present in it (III.4).

work-centre-of-life.rationale: Says work never held a central position in traditional societies and modernity wrongly made it a value in itself (III.8).

notes: Answers rest on the 1999 manifesto, which differs from earlier racialist and later Faye-era writings; scholars read the movement more harshly than its self-description (ethnic homogeneity against the manifesto's rejection of exclusion), so the ethnic-nation answer is a split. Metapolitics (culture before politics) has no statement and the manifesto itself denies it is a strategy of hegemony.
